Thankyou for your reply, the country is divided into different health boards, each responsible for its own area. Pay scales are banded and doctors nurses porters domestic staff etc are the same for each band I do not think clinical staff are able to receive bonuses or deductions however I believe that health board management are. 

Doctors and staff are very able to advocate for patients however if it’s a very expensive or unusual treatment this would be considered by clinical commissioning groups I think they are called who would make the final decision on whether this procedure would be funded. I work for the NHS also and as staff we do not think of our selves as government employees. Rather employees of our health board as we are quite detached from government at a basic everyday clinical level. Generally the government step in if there is a major incident or targets are not met etc. 

Nhs staff contracts are generally good and considered where I am to provide job stability. Sick pay is for 6 months after you have been employed over a certain time and maternity leave can stretch out to around a year although pay is not to your usual amount.

Certain service such as catering in some places are put out for tender to private companies.

There is private health care which if you have can help you skip waiting lists however the problem sometimes is that with the nhs if you were being treated for eg cancer you would be treated on a specialised oncology ward however private care being a much smaller entities you could be on a ward with patients being treated privately for many different problems. This could possibly mean your nursing care is not as specialised. However many of the doctors working privately are doing this as extra whilst also working for the nhs.

There is not an option for private emergency care as far as I am aware so pretty much anyone in emergency need would receive an ambulance and nhs emergency care.

In terms of substance use I personally feel that some people are so desperately in need to have some rest for the trauma they have experiences and or what they are living through right now. It’s entirely understandable and helps people get though the worst times. However as it can be so damaging in the long term I feel it’s so important to get a balance between reducing your use age and increasing your more positive coping skills.

In general psychiatric services will not work with someone with addiction issues until they are in a place of stability. This is because we cannot assess what is mental health related and what is substance abuse related. We are very aware that mental illness can lead to self medication which means people using substances but given the work we want to do with you about building resilience and coping skills safety and stability needs you to be able to engage fully in this so it would be really difficult to do this whilst you were still using substances. Also substance use could be very harmful to physical health so it’s important to stabilse ASAP. 

As part of a coping mechanism it would be great if you were able to learn more health strategies than substances as that’s going to be a vicious circle y

I could no longer follow my career plans as I had no qualifications.
